(1) Giglio, Maggiori, and Sturgess (2015) use a hedonic regression to show that Singaporean households pay a premium for long-term leases.

(a) in Singapore the vast majority of five digit zip code level variation in lease length is due to location rather than to the lease length itself; (b) the vast majority of the variation in location is unobserved by the hedonic regression; (c) in the hedonic regression, location is measured by five digit zip code; (d) the vast majority (9.2%) of five digit zipcodes in Singapore display no within variation in residential lease length.

the vast majority of zip codes displayed no variation in lease length and that the authors’ conclusions about lease length and price do not hold when the analysis is conducted in a way that accounts for this.
